title: Outage: a cleanup job deleted the payments namespace and its hand-made Secrets

lines.text: 10:30 page: namespace payments is gone (deleted 09:40 by the cleanup job); the payments batch runs at 11:00
Runbook: nightly etcd snapshot at 02:00 to /var/backups/etcd/snap-0200.db. payments' Secrets were created by hand and are not in Git.
11:00: the payments batch could not run

objective: Back up and restore etcd with etcdctl snapshot save and etcdutl snapshot restore using the right certificates and endpoint, and bring the static pod back up on the restored data

sources.cite: Kubernetes documentation, Operating etcd clusters for Kubernetes
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-16 (the second part of the page). Relevant text: snapshot save with 'ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl --endpoints=https://127.0.0.1:2379' and '--cacert=<trusted-ca-file> --cert=<cert-file> --key=<key-file>', the paths taken from the etcd Pod's description; 'etcdutl --data-dir <data-dir-location> snapshot restore snapshot.db', a directory the restore creates; 'If any API servers are running in your cluster, you should not attempt to restore instances of etcd': stop all API server instances, restore, restart them; if the data directory changes, change '/etc/kubernetes/manifests/etcd.yaml's volumes.hostPath.path for name: etcd-data'; verify with 'etcdutl --write-out=table snapshot status snapshot.db'; restart kube-scheduler, kube-controller-manager and kubelet after a restore, since they lose their leader lock.

Fictional cluster and company. Command output is an authored rendering of kubectl, etcdctl, etcdutl, crictl and systemctl output, shortened. That a restore returns the cluster to the snapshot's state, so later changes must be re-applied, follows from what a snapshot is; the times are the author's.

brief.situation: You are the Kubernetes administrator for Kestrel Lending, a fictional lender. At 10:30 the payments team pages: namespace payments is gone. A cleanup job deleted it at 09:40. The payments batch runs at 11:00. cp1 is a single kubeadm control plane node with a stacked etcd.
handover: A nightly job saves an etcd snapshot at 02:00 to /var/backups/etcd/snap-0200.db.
payments' Secrets (bank API credentials) were created by hand and are not in Git; the shop team deployed promo from Git at 08:00.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the diagram shows the API server, etcd, the namespaces at stake and the batch.
Each command takes a minute or two; the clock moves only when you act or wait.
When you close the outage, you write the record and explain your reasoning.

source.note: The payments batch runs at 11:00, 30 minutes after the 10:30 page.

source.note: How many minutes each command or task takes, and when the fictional problem spreads, are teaching simplifications for exam practice, not measured values.

writeup.question: For the record: why a restore, how you did it safely, and what the restore cost.

parts.label: Why restore
parts.criteria: Recognizes that the Secrets exist nowhere but etcd, so recreating from Git is not enough.
parts.modelAnswer: The cleanup job deleted the namespace; its Secrets were made by hand and are not in Git, so only the 02:00 etcd snapshot holds them.

parts.label: Safely
parts.criteria: Verifies the snapshot, saves today's state with the right endpoint and certificates, stops the API server, restores to a new directory and points the etcd manifest at it, then restarts the API server and the components that lose their leader lock.
parts.modelAnswer: snapshot status read the 02:00 snapshot; etcdctl with the endpoint and the CA, certificate and key from the etcd Pod saved pre-restore.db; with kube-apiserver.yaml moved out I restored to /var/lib/etcd-restore and changed the etcd-data hostPath; then the API server came back and I restarted kubelet, the scheduler and the controller manager.

parts.label: Cost
parts.criteria: Re-applies what changed after the snapshot and verifies before the batch.
parts.modelAnswer: The restore took the cluster back to 02:00, so I synced the 08:00 promo deployment from Git; kubectl showed payments and its Secrets back before 11:00.

source.note: The payments batch runs at 11:00; the scenario's own timing.
No second fault: a reset control plane, a restore under a running API server, or changes lost since 02:00.

noProgress.rationale: Closing without payments and its Secrets leaves the batch unable to run.

expertPath.text: Namespace gone; the etcd Pod's flags give the endpoint, CA, certificate, key and data directory; snapshot status reads the 02:00 snapshot; etcdctl with those flags saves pre-restore.db.
Move kube-apiserver.yaml out; etcdutl restore to /var/lib/etcd-restore; point the etcd-data hostPath at it; move the API server manifest back.
Restart kubelet, the scheduler and the controller manager; sync the 08:00 promo deployment from Git; verify payments and its Secrets.

restored.headline: Good: the documented restore, and nothing else lost
restored.body: You restored only because the Secrets lived nowhere else, kept today's state first, followed the order the documentation gives (API server stopped, new data directory, manifest, restart), and re-applied what the snapshot did not have.

gaps.headline: Back, with gaps
gaps.body: The criteria show what was left: the snapshot check, today's state, the component restarts, or the 08:00 changes the restore removed.

broken.headline: Control plane damaged
broken.body: kubeadm reset deletes etcd's data; swapping etcd's data under a running API server leaves its caches and etcd disagreeing. Stop every API server, then restore.

batchMissed.headline: The batch could not run
batchMissed.body: Recreating the namespace from Git brings the Deployments back without the hand-made Secrets. The 02:00 snapshot held them.

time_up.headline: Time up
time_up.body: No record was written before the run's hard limit.

scoring.modelReasoning: The cleanup job deleted payments, whose Secrets were made by hand and exist only in etcd, so recreating from Git is not enough. Take the endpoint, CA, certificate and key from the etcd Pod; check the 02:00 snapshot with etcdutl snapshot status and save today's state with etcdctl using those flags. Stop the API server by moving its manifest out, restore with etcdutl to a new data directory (the live one is refused), point the etcd-data hostPath in etcd.yaml at it, bring the API server back, and restart kubelet, the scheduler and the controller manager. The restore takes the cluster back to 02:00, so sync the 08:00 promo deployment from Git, and verify payments and its Secrets before 11:00.
